title: Festive Season Lending Readiness Checklist for NBFCs
summary: A festive season lending checklist for NBFCs and fintech lenders: prepare KYC, penny drop, eNACH and UPI Autopay, and RBI rules before Diwali.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


##


What is festive season lending?


Festive season lending is credit offered at the point of purchase during India’s sale and gifting season, from Big Billion Days and the Great Indian Festival through Dhanteras and Diwali. It is mostly small-ticket, short-tenure and instant: cardless EMI, buy now pay later, credit lines on UPI and consumer durable loans, approved in seconds and repaid over 3 to 12 months.


The defining trait is the demand curve. Volumes do not rise gradually. They arrive in a few days, all at once, and every onboarding, verification and repayment step has to hold up under that spike.


##


Why is festive readiness an infrastructure problem?


Because festive demand is predictable, and credit models rarely break under it. The steps around the credit decision do: onboarding, bank verification and mandate setup. These are the stages where a spike in traffic turns into drop-offs at checkout and bounced first EMIs weeks later.


The scale is documented. In the opening two days of the 2026 festive sales, online platforms recorded about ₹24,200 crore in GMV, roughly 6x the normal daily run rate, and electronics orders ran at nearly 14x normal daily levels ([Redseer via IANS, October 2026](https://telanganatoday.com/festive-sales-e-commerce-platforms-clock-rs-24000-crore-in-two-days) ;[Redseer via PTI, October 2026](https://yourstory.com/2026/10/ecomm-firms-goods-worth-rs-24k-cr-first-two-days-festive-sales-redseer) ).


The mix of buyers makes verification harder. Redseer estimates that about two-thirds of the 6 to 6.5 crore shoppers in those two days came from Tier 2 cities and rural areas, and that first-time online shoppers doubled year on year ([Redseer via PTI, October 2026](https://yourstory.com/2026/10/ecomm-firms-goods-worth-rs-24k-cr-first-two-days-festive-sales-redseer) ). Many applicants are new to credit, with thin files and first-time digital KYC.


The payment rails carry the same surge. UPI processed a then-record 20.7 billion transactions in October 2025, the festive month ([NPCI data via Business Today, 2025](https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/banking/story/upi-hits-record-754-mn-transactions-in-a-single-day-monthly-volume-surges-to-207-bn-in-october-500469-2025-11-01) ), and monthly volume has since reached 24.51 billion in August 2026 ([NPCI data via Outlook Business, 2026](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/upi-transactions-near-record-level-of-rs-298-lakh-cr-in-aug-volume-at-all-time-high-of-2451-bn) ). Disbursements, penny drop checks and mandate registrations all ride on that infrastructure.


An approval engine can add capacity ahead of a sale. A KYC timeout, a penny drop that fails at a bank cut-off, or an eNACH mandate that never registers cannot be fixed that week, which is why lenders prepare for them before the sale.


##


What should a festive lending checklist cover?


It should cover eight stages, in the order a borrower meets them. Each stage below explains what it is, why it strains under festive volume, and what ready looks like.


###


1. How do you keep KYC and onboarding from failing at peak?


Give every identity check a timeout and a fallback. KYC is the first step of any festive loan, so a slow check shows up as an abandoned application. Many festive applicants are first-time digital borrowers with thin credit files, so clear error messages and a retry path matter as much as speed.


**Ready looks like this** : onboarding load-tested at 6x or more of normal daily volume, with a fallback for each check (PAN, Aadhaar-based eKYC, CKYC fetch, liveness) and only the data you need collected, with consent. Decentro’s KYC & Onboarding lets you run these checks through one integration.


###


2. Why does bank account verification come before disbursal?


Because a loan sent to a wrong or inactive account is expensive to reverse, and the same account later carries the repayment mandate. The standard check is penny drop verification: a small test credit, typically ₹1, that returns the account holder’s name so it can be matched against KYC.


**Ready looks like this** : every borrower verified before disbursal, a name-match rule agreed with risk (near-matches go to manual review), and a plan for bank downtime and cut-offs. Decentro’s bank account verification API covers penny drop and name match.


###


3. How do you protect the credit decision when traffic spikes?


Decide in advance what happens when a data source is slow or down. The credit engine is usually the part lenders already trust, so the failures tend to arrive around it, such as a bureau call that times out.


**Ready looks like this** : timeouts on bureau and bank-statement calls, a written fallback for each (reject, manual review or lower limit), pre-approved limits for existing customers, and offers that show the lender, amount, tenor, APR, charges and a Key Facts Statement link. A credit line on UPI, where a pre-sanctioned limit is spent through a UPI app, shortens the journey further, but it still depends on a fast, reliable limit decision.


###


4. Should festive EMI use eNACH or UPI Autopay?


Use both, routed by ticket size. A mandate is the borrower’s one-time permission for automatic EMI debits.[UPI Autopay](https://decentro.tech/resources/upi-autopay-apis) is instant but capped per debit, while an[eNACH](https://decentro.tech/resources/enach-apis) mandate handles larger tickets but takes several working days to activate.


**UPI Autopay** **eNACH**


Setup time Instant, approved in the UPI app About 3 to 4 working days


Amount limit ₹15,000 per debit without extra authentication; ₹1 lakh for specified categories Higher; commonly up to ₹10 lakh for e-mandates


Best for Small-ticket, high-volume EMIs Larger tickets and longer tenures


Sources:[Razorpay](https://razorpay.com/blog/upi-autopay-vs-enach-comparison/) ,[PhonePe](https://business.phonepe.com/articles/how-to-accept-subscription-payments-in-india-upi-auto-pay-vs-e-nach-vs-cards) (2026). Limits change, so confirm the cap for your category with your sponsor bank.


**Ready looks like this** : a mandate type chosen by ticket size, a fallback if the first mandate fails, a clear rule on whether disbursal waits for mandate confirmation, and pre-debit notifications and retry rules set before the first EMI falls due. Decentro Recurring Payments is where eNACH and UPI Autopay mandates are created and managed.


###


5. How do you disburse thousands of loans in a sale window?


Use instant payment rails with reconciliation built in, because manual batches cannot keep pace when approvals arrive in bursts. Disbursal should go to the borrower’s own account, as the Digital Lending Directions require with limited exceptions, so confirm your checkout financing structure with compliance.


**Ready looks like this** : pre-funded payout accounts, idempotency keys so a retry never pays a loan twice, status tracked by webhook through to a final state, and an alternate rail for failed payouts. Decentro’s Instant Payouts handles disbursal over real-time rails with status callbacks.


###


6. What do the RBI Digital Lending Directions require at checkout?


Three requirements bite hardest during a sale: a Key Facts Statement before the loan is finalised, a cooling-off period of at least one day, and a written agreement with every lending service provider. The Directions were issued on 8 May 2025 ([RBI](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/FS_Notification.aspx?Id=12848) ).


The Key Facts Statement must be in plain language, with a digitally signed copy sent to the borrower ([Kochhar & Co.](https://www.mondaq.com/article/1636908/digital-lending-directions-2025) ). The lender’s board sets the cooling-off period, with a minimum of one day, and the borrower can exit without penalty, though a disclosed one-time processing fee may be retained ([AZB & Partners](https://www.mondaq.com/india/financial-services/1651878/rbi-digital-lending-directions-2025-same-same-but-different) ).


**Ready looks like this** : all three tested end to end, including mandate cancellation and refunds when a borrower exits. This is a summary, not legal advice, so check the current text with your compliance team.


###


7. How do you stop fraud without blocking genuine festive buyers?


Tune controls for a surge of first-time users: layered checks and velocity limits work better than blanket declines.


**Ready looks like this** : alerts for many applications from one device, phone number or bank account, name matching across KYC, PAN and bank account, real-time watch on mandate and payout anomalies; and rules reviewed every few hours for the first 48 hours, since the opening two days carry the peak.


###


8. How do you prepare for post-festive collections?


Start before the sale ends, because the first EMI usually falls about a month later, and mandate health at that point largely decides early delinquency.


**Ready looks like this** : first-debit success tracked by mandate type, retry timing for failed debits, an alternate route such as a payment link or second mandate, pre-debit notifications as the RBI e-mandate framework requires, and early outreach in the borrower’s language within RBI fair-practice norms.


##


How does cardless EMI work at checkout?


Cardless EMI lets a shopper pay in instalments without a credit card: the lender approves an instant limit at checkout using KYC and bank checks, the shopper picks a tenure, and repayment runs through a mandate.


Each step maps to a stage in the eight stages above.


1. The shopper selects cardless EMI at checkout and enters a mobile number plus PAN or date of birth (stage 1).
2. The lender runs KYC and a credit check and returns an instant limit (stages 1 and 3).
3. The shopper sees the Key Facts Statement, picks a tenure and consents; the cooling-off period starts (stage 6).
4. The borrower’s bank account is verified, and a UPI Autopay or eNACH mandate is registered (stages 2 and 4).
5. The loan is disbursed, and the order is confirmed; the first EMI is debited on schedule (stages 5 and 8).


The whole journey has to finish in minutes, which is why each handoff needs a timeout and a fallback.


##


How ready is your lending stack?


Here is a table to help you understand and track your festival readiness.


**Stage** **You are ready when**


1.[KYC and onboarding](https://decentro.tech/products/kyc-onboarding) Every check has a timeout and fallback, and the flow is load-tested at 6x or more


2. Bank account verification Penny drop and name match run on every borrower, with a manual review path


3. Credit decision Each data source has a fallback policy, and offers show APR, charges and a KFS link


4. Mandate setup Mandates are routed by ticket size, with a fallback type and a disbursal rule


5. Disbursement Payouts are pre-funded, idempotent and reconciled, with an alternate rail


6. Compliance KFS, cooling-off exit and lending service provider agreements are tested end-to-end


7. Fraud Velocity and name-match rules are live, with a named on-call owner


8. Collections First-debit success is tracked, with retries and an alternate payment route

# Frequently asked questions


**What is cardless EMI?**


Cardless EMI is instalment credit offered at checkout without a credit card. The lender approves an instant limit using KYC and bank data, and repayment runs through a mandate such as UPI Autopay or eNACH.


**What is a penny drop verification?**


A penny drop sends a small test credit, typically ₹1, to a bank account and returns the account holder’s name. Lenders use it to confirm the account exists and matches the borrower before disbursing or registering a mandate.


**Should festive EMI use eNACH or UPI Autopay?**


Use both, routed by ticket size. UPI Autopay activates instantly but has a ₹15,000 per-debit limit without extra authentication, while eNACH supports larger amounts but takes several working days to activate.


**What is the cooling-off period under the RBI Digital Lending Directions, 2025?**


It is a window in which a borrower can exit a digital loan without penalty. The lender’s board sets the length, subject to a minimum of one day, and a disclosed one-time processing fee may be retained.


**What is a Key Facts Statement?**


A Key Facts Statement is a standardised summary of a loan’s terms, charges, APR and repayment schedule. Under the Directions, the borrower must receive it in a digitally signed form before the loan is finalised.


**When should lenders start festive readiness work?**


Start load tests and mandate checks several weeks before the sale opens, and freeze changes in the final week. Demand peaks within the first two days, so there is little time to fix issues once the sale is live.
